'''Alexander Maurice Acker''' (born January 21, 1983) is an American-Italian<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=ACK-ALE-83 |title=Alex Acker Naz. Sportiva: ITA . |access-date=2017-07-18 |language=it |archive-date=2018-03-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180301230125/http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=ACK-ALE-83 |url-status=dead }}</ref> former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Pepperdine University]]. Acker was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] as the final pick of the [[2005 NBA draft]] and spent two seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) with the Pistons and [[Los Angeles Clippers]].

==College career==
Acker attended [[Pepperdine University]], where he played [[college basketball]] with the [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine Waves]], from 2002 to 2005.

==Professional career==

===NBA===
After college, Acker was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]], with the last pick in the second round (60th overall) of the [[2005 NBA draft]]. He played with the Pistons in 5 games, during the 2005–06 season, and he was also assigned to the [[NBA Development League]]'s [[Fayetteville Patriots]], on February 27, 2006.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090630114242/http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/acker_060302.html Pistons Assign Acker To Fayetteville.]</ref>

===Europe===
From 2006 to 2008, Acker played with the Greek club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], for whom he averaged 14.3 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.4 assists, and 1.8 steals, in 22 games played ([[Euroleague 2006–07|2006–07 EuroLeague season]]), and with the Spanish club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|AXA FC Barcelona]], averaging 5.5 points, 1.9 rebounds and 0.7 assists and 0.7 steals, in 22 games played ([[Euroleague 2007–08|2007–08 EuroLeague season]]).<ref name="signedacker">[https://web.archive.org/web/20081006122333/http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/acker_080929.html Pistons Sign Free Agent Guard Alex Acker.]</ref>

===Return to NBA===
On September 29, 2008, it was announced that Acker had signed a deal with his former [[NBA]] team, the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref name="signedacker" /> On February 16, 2009, Acker was traded by Detroit to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], along with a second-round draft pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]], in exchange for a conditional second-round draft pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Clippers Acquire Alex Acker From Detroit Pistons. |url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/acker_090216.html |work=NBA.com |date=2009-02-16 |access-date=2009-02-17| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090301104601/http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/acker_090216.html| archive-date= 1 March 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref> This trade was completed primarily for the Pistons to clear [[NBA salary cap|salary cap]] space, and to open up a roster spot for trade flexibility.<ref>[http://www.detnews.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20090216/SPORTS0102/902160416/1004/SPORTS Pistons get 2013 second-rounder, cap space for Acker.]</ref>

===Return to Europe===
On August 22, 2009, Acker signed with [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Armani Jeans Milano]] of Italy's [[Lega Basket Serie A|LBA]], for the 2009–10 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/78728/milano-signs-alex-acker.html Milano signs Alex Acker.]</ref><ref>[http://www.interbasket.net/news/3678/2009/08/23/alex-acker-departs-nba-returns-to-europe/ Alex Acker departs NBA, returns to Europe.]</ref> In September 2010, Acker signed a one-year deal with [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans]] of France's [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>[http://thehoop.blogspot.com/2010/09/le-mans-signed-alex-acker.html Le Mans signed Alex Acker.]</ref> On June 30, 2011, he re-signed with Le Mans for one more season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/86923/alex-acker-re-signs-with-le-mans.html Alex Acker re-signs with Le Mans.]</ref>

On October 16, 2012, Acker signed a one-year contract with [[Asseco Prokom Gdynia]] of Poland's [[Polish Basketball League|PLK]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/100875/asseco-prokom-gdynia-adds-veteran-acker ASSECO PROKOM GDYNIA adds veteran Acker.]</ref> On December 21, 2012, he parted ways with Prokom.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/poland/97621/asseco-prokom-gdynia-alex-acker-part-ways.html Asseco Prokom Gdynia, Alex Acker part ways.]</ref> On February 14, 2013, he signed a two-month deal with [[Boulazac Basket Dordogne|Boulazac Dordogne]] of France.<ref>{{cite web|title=Boulazac signs Alex Acker to a 2-month deal.|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/99194/boulazac-signs-alex-acker-to-a-2-month-deal.html|work=Sportando.net|access-date=3 May 2013}}</ref>

On May 2, 2013, he signed with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] of France, for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=ASVEL signs Alex Acker.|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/france/55076/asvel-signs-alex-acker.html|work=Sportando.net|access-date=3 May 2013}}</ref> On June 28, 2013, he signed a one-year deal with [[Limoges CSP|Limoges]] of France.<ref>{{cite news|title=Limoges signs Alex Acker.|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/france/58025/limoges-signs-alex-acker.html|access-date=27 August 2013|newspaper=Sportando.net|date=28 June 2013}}</ref> With Limoges, he won the [[2013–14 Pro A season|2013–14 LNB Pro A]] championship, and he was named the [[LNB Pro A Finals MVP|MVP of the Finals]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Limoges, champions for the 10th time! |url=http://www.eurohoops.net/2014/06/league-action/50414 |access-date=June 13, 2014 |work=eurohoops.net |date=June 6, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140610150528/http://www.eurohoops.net/2014/06/league-action/50414 |archive-date=June 10, 2014 }}</ref>

On October 25, 2014, Acker signed with [[İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyespor (basketball)|İstanbul BB]] of Turkey.<ref>{{cite news|title=Istanbul BSB officially signs Alex Acker.|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/138845/istanbul-bsb-officially-signs-alex-acker.html|access-date=October 25, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=October 25, 2014}}</ref> On December 29, 2014, he returned to France, and signed with his former team, [[ASVEL Basket]].<ref>{{cite news|title=ASVEL Villeurbanne lands Alex Acker.|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/146679/asvel-villeurbanne-lands-alex-acker.html|access-date=December 29, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=December 29, 2014}}</ref> On July 10, 2015, he parted ways with ASVEL.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/168078/asvel-parted-ways-with-amara-sy-alex-acker-and-georgi-joseph.html ASVEL parted ways with Amara Sy, Alex Acker and Georgi Joseph.]</ref>

On August 26, 2015, Acker signed with [[S.S. Felice Scandone|Sidigas Avellino]] for the 2015–16 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/173950/sidigas-avellino-announces-alex-acker.html Sidigas Avellino announces Alex Acker.]</ref> On October 27, 2016, Acker signed with [[Pallacanestro Cantù]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/215580/pallacanestro-cantu-signs-alex-acker.html Pallacanestro Cantù signs Alex Acker.]</ref> On October 25, 2017, Acker signed with [[Apollon Patras B.C.|Apollon Patras]], of the [[Greek A2 Basket League|Greek 2nd Division]].<ref>[https://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/251404/alex-acker-inks-with-apollon-patras.html Alex Acker inks with Apollon Patras.]</ref>
